title: KV hit signal reconciliation and minimal-delta evaluation tests
creator: Lena Park
description: Problem: We observe that enabling or tuning KV/prefix cache heuristics sometimes produces small but meaningful output deltas when a request is served from cache vs cold path. Prior work covered detection and bulk audits; this ticket focuses on reproducible reconciliation of the "hit signal" (the runtime's indication that a request used prefix/KV cached state) and a minimal-delta evaluation harness for gating config and model changes. Goal: produce a lightweight test suite + reconciliation tooling that explains whether a hit-induced delta is an acceptable semantic no-op (e.g., punctuation/formatting) or a behavioral regression requiring rollback. The output must integrate into CI/canary gating and provide human-readable explainability artifacts for PM/DS/Oncall reviewers.
steps: 1) Define canonical 'reconciliation' signature: token-aligned edit distance, normalized semantic similarity (SBERT cosine), and a delta classification heuristic (formatting|paraphrase|content-loss|hallucination).
2) Assemble a minimal golden set: 2k user-like prompts sampled from production intents across chat/generation/QA/structured output. Label ~200 edge cases (multi-turn, function-calling, long-prefix).

3) Implement a lightweight harness that replays requests through both cold path and hit path (shadowing + deterministic seed) and captures: model logits, tokens, response, attention-check signatures, and hit metadata (cache keys, prefix length, cache age).
4) Compute per-sample reconciliation report: token-diff, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, SBERT similarity, and a taxonomy tag plus a compact explanation sentence describing the delta cause probability.
5) Add gates to canary pipeline: fail if >0.5% of high-severity deltas (content-loss/hallucination) or if median SBERT similarity for top-traffic intents drops below 0.92.
6) Wire up dashboard & alert: cliff-notes for SRE/PM with sample failing queries + links to replay artifacts and suggested rollback commit.
7) Run a pilot on runtime-1.20 canary with two config deltas: increased prefix-eviction threshold and kernel scheduling change; iterate on thresholds.
8) Document runbook for oncall: how to interpret reconciliation reports, immediate mitigations (temporarily disable caching or set hit-probability throttle), and follow-up postmortem steps.
9) Post-pilot: bake harness into nightly regression runs and expose a lightweight API for product/DS to run targeted recon checks before model/config rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation harness runs end-to-end in <30m for 2k samples on CI infra and produces an artifact bundle (JSON + zipped traces).
Automated delta classifier achieves >=85% precision on held-out labeled edge set for 'content-loss' vs 'formatting' categories.
Canary gate triggers correctly on pilot configs: we detect and surface at least one meaningful regression during pilot where manual inspection agrees (>90% reviewer agreement).
Dashboard tile surfaces top-20 failing queries with sample diffs and links to replay records for debugging.
Runbook documented and reviewed by oncall, PM, and a DS reviewer.
risks: Sampling bias in golden set could miss rare intents leading to escapes in production.
Non-determinism in runtime (e.g., floating-point kernel reorder) may produce noisy signals increasing false positives.
Cost: capturing logits and traces for large replay sets increases storage and CI time unless we limit to token-level hashes + compressed diffs.
Overly strict gates could block safe rollouts; thresholds need careful tuning and escalation paths.
monitoring_queries: ELK query for failing reconciliation samples: index=kv-replay-* AND delta_class:"content-loss" | top 100 by traffic_count

SQL snippet for daily delta rate: SELECT date, intent, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delta_severity='high')/COUNT(*) as high_delta_rate FROM kv_reconciliations WHERE date >= current_date - interval '7 days' GROUP BY date, intent;
Pager alert rule: trigger if 10-min rolling window high_delta_rate > 0.5% for top-10 intents
SLO check: compare median SBERT similarity on canary vs baseline; alert if drop > 0.03
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal pilot - run harness against nightly builds and a copy of production sample traffic (shadowed).
Phase 1: canary - enable cache heuristics change for 5% of traffic with reconciliation gate active. Monitor 48h.
Phase 2: incremental rollout - 5% -> 25% -> 50% with manual checkpoints and automated gate evaluation at each step.
Phase 3: full rollout if canary metrics stable for 7 days and no high-severity regressions exceed threshold.
runbook: If canary gate fires and delta_count_high > threshold: immediately flip 'kv-prefix-cache' to conservative mode for affected region.
Collect and tag failing samples via reconciliation artifact -> open a triage ticket assigned to runtime-oncall + model-owner.
If >5% of top-traffic intents impacted: rollback to previous runtime commit and notify product/ops mailing list.
For suspected non-determinism: run deterministic replay with fixed seeds and capture low-level kernel logs (link in artifact bundle).
